issues.legal_issue: A decision of a High Court on a statutory appeal from an arbitrator’s award remains an arbitral decision and is not appealable as an ordinary court judgment, decree, or order.
material_facts: A statutory reference was made to an arbitrator to determine compensation for requisitioned property after the parties could not agree on the amount.
The High Court heard an appeal from the arbitrator’s award and varied the compensation.
Both sides sought to appeal the High Court’s decision to the Supreme Court under ordinary civil appellate provisions and the applicable Letters Patent.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s decision was an award made in the course of the statutory arbitration, not a judgment, decree, or order appealable under the ordinary civil appellate provisions or the Letters Patent. Both appeals were therefore incompetent.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 19(1)(b), 19(1)(f), and 19(1)(g) of the Defence of India Act, the compensation dispute was referred to an arbitrator and the statutory appeal from the award remained part of the arbitration proceedings. Section 46 of the Arbitration Act, 1940, reflects that statutory arbitrations generally stand on the footing of arbitrations by agreement. Whether a decision is appealable under sections 109 and 110 of the Code of Civil Procedure or the Letters Patent depends on whether the court acted in its ordinary civil jurisdiction or as a designated arbitral authority. The Court relied on Rangoon Botatoung Company v. The Collector, Rangoon; The Special Officer, Salsette Building Sites v. Dossabhai Bezonji; The Special Officer, Salsette Building Sites v. Dossabhai Basenji Motiwala; Manavikraman Tirumalpad v. The Collector of the Nilgris; Secretary of State for India in Council v. Hindusthan Co-operative Insurance Society Limited; National Telephone Company Limited v. Postmaster General; Secretary of State for India v. Chelikani Rama Rao; and Kollegal Silk Filatures Ltd. v. Province of Madras.

predicates.statutory_arbitration_proceeding: A statute refers a dispute to an arbitrator for determination.
predicates.appeal_from_arbitrator_award: A party brings the statutorily provided appeal against the arbitrator’s award before a High Court.
predicates.appellate_stage_continues_same_proceedin: The High Court hears the appeal as a further stage of the original arbitral proceeding rather than as a newly instituted ordinary civil case.

issues.definition: When a statutory arbitration proceeds to a High Court appeal that continues the same proceeding, the High Court’s decision is not appealable as an ordinary court judgment.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court cannot use inherited special-leave jurisdiction to entertain an appeal from a High Court decision that is an arbitral award rather than a judgment, decree, or order in a civil case.
material_facts: The proposed appeals challenged the High Court’s decision in an appeal from an arbitrator’s award.
The appellants argued that the Supreme Court could grant leave under jurisdiction inherited from the former Federal Court even if ordinary appellate routes were unavailable.
issues.conclusion: The Court could not grant special leave through the asserted inherited jurisdiction because the challenged decision was an award, not a judgment, decree, or order within the relevant jurisdictional requirement. The appeals were dismissed as incompetent.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(a)(ii) of the Federal Court (Enlargement of Jurisdiction) Act, 1948, empowered the Federal Court to grant leave only for a proposed appeal against a judgment, and section 2(b) defined that term as a judgment, decree, or order of a High Court in a civil case. The Court held that the asserted power had not passed to it under Article 135 of the Constitution in relation to a decision that did not meet that requirement.

predicates.special_leave_sought_under_inherited_jur: A party asks the Supreme Court to grant special leave by relying on jurisdiction inherited from a former court.
predicates.proposed_appeal_is_from_statutory_arbitr: The proposed appeal challenges a High Court decision made in an appeal from a statutory arbitrator’s award.
predicates.challenged_decision_is_an_award_not_a_co: The challenged decision is an arbitral award rather than a judgment, decree, or order made by the High Court in its ordinary civil jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When special leave is sought through inherited jurisdiction for an appeal from a statutory arbitration appeal, it is unavailable if the challenged decision is an award rather than a court judgment.
